title: No simple formula describes many steps of rule 30 evolution

fields.label: Label
fields.value: No simple formula describes many steps of rule 30 evolution

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Minimal Boolean formulas (in disjunctive normal form or in Nand operations) for the outcome of rule 30 grow rapidly with the number of steps, unlike those for simple rules such as 90 and 254, indicating that no simple formula describes rule 30 evolution and that, in most cases, cellular automaton patterns have no simple mathematical formula.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 10: Processes of Perception and Analysis

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: So even if one allows rather general structure, the evidence is that in the end there is no way to set up any simple formula that will describe the outcome of evolution for a system like rule 30.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 10, “Processes of Perception and Analysis”; section “Human Thinking” (from p. 620), p. 620. Scope: formula representations of cellular automaton evolution, especially rule 30

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch10-18: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.70

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing computation can reproduce formula-size growth for many steps and representations. The unrestricted conclusion that no simple formula exists requires formal complexity lower bounds and cannot be inferred completely from finite cases.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compute exact minimal formula sizes for bounded rule-30 light cones in specified bases and compare growth with rules 90 and 254; separately seek asymptotic lower bounds. Rapid finite growth supports the evidence claim, while a compact general formula refutes the conclusion.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Simplicity depends on the allowed representation language.

Exact formula minimization grows combinatorially.

Finite growth does not prove an asymptotic impossibility theorem.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Formula size after a few steps is a finite computation, and the contrast with rules 90 and 254 is well defined. Those small-n sizes can be recomputed and either continue the rapid growth Wolfram reports or break it. They do not prove that no simple formula exists for arbitrary step counts, nor the further claim about most cellular automata.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compute minimal disjunctive-normal-form and Nand formula sizes for the state of rule 30 after t steps, and compare growth with rules 90 and 254. Rapid growth relative to those rules at accessible t supports the small-n evidence; a compact formula at large t, or slow growth, would refute 'no simple formula'.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Growth of one normal form does not rule out a compact formula in some other language.

Exact minimal formulas become intractable as the light-cone width grows, so only small step counts are feasible.
